# Subsetting Astrocytes from All Celltype-Seurat

This is the first script of this project. In this project, I analysed single-nuclei RNA sequencing (snRNAseq) data of post-mortem spinal cord tissue of 20 ALS patients and 4 controls, focusing on astrocytes. In this script, I will open the full dataset (with all celltypes), examine the astrocytes (e.g. what proportion of total cells they form per sample), and subset the astrocytes.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-01-setup
#| include: false
# Manage settings for code chunks throughout the document
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Helper functions

<details>

<summary>*Click here to view the helper functions of this document*</summary>

### save_plot()

This document will display all images I make. However, I also want to save these images on disk - both as a .pdf file and .png file. This function saves both; I only need to provide the gplot-object, the name for the file (without filetype extension!) and optionally the width and heigth of the figure. 
```{r}
#| label: chunk-04-helper-save-plot
# file.path provides the path, but I need to use paste0 to concatenate .png
save_plot <- function(p, filename, width = 10, height = 6) {
  png_file <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".png"))
  ggsave(png_file, p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
  pdf_file <- file.path(dir_fig, paste0(filename, ".pdf"))
  ggsave(pdf_file, p, width = width, height = height, dpi = 150)
}
```

### calc_freq()

In the section **Visualization Astrocyte Frequency**, I'll make barplots with the frequencies of cell types per sample. I will create figures which show the frequency of all cell types, but also one which just shows *astrocytes vs non-astrocytes*. To do this efficiently, I created the function calc_freq which can calculate both.


```{r}
#| label: chunk-05-helper-calc-freq
calc_freq <- function(metadata, col_celltype, col_sample = "AnonymousID") {
  freq_table <- table(
    metadata[, col_celltype],
    metadata[, col_sample]
  ) |>
    as.data.frame()
  colnames(freq_table) <- c("Celltype", "Sample", "Frequency")
  # Rearrange the columns so they are in a sensible order; as sample numbers are
  # given with single digits for single digit character, it's currently in the
  # order ALS1, ALS10, ALS11, ..., ALS19, ALS2, ALS20, ALS3, ALS4 etc. and does
  # not count up like we humans would.
  freq_table <- freq_table |>
    mutate(
      Sample = fct_relevel(
        Sample, str_sort(unique(as.character(Sample)), numeric = TRUE)
      )
    )
  freq_table
}
```

### bar_freq()

`bar_freq()` creates the visualizations of the same section. The argument freq_type becomes the argument to position in geom_bar: "stack" makes it absolute, "fill" makes it proportional. I added the argument just_astro because I want to manually colour the plot red vs grey in case of the astrocyte vs non-astrocyte plot. The function assumes you provide the output of calc_freq() as input.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-06-helper-bar-freq
# The argument freq_type becomes the argument to position in geom_bar.
# "stack" makes it absolute, "fill" makes it proportional.
bar_freq <- function(freq_table, freq_type = "fill", just_astro = FALSE) {
  p_bar <- ggplot(freq_table, aes(fill = Celltype, y = Frequency, x = Sample)) +
    geom_bar(position = freq_type, stat = "identity") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) # otherwise unreadable x-axis

  if (just_astro) {
    p_bar <- p_bar + scale_fill_manual(values = c("#EF2400", "grey"))
  }

  p_bar
}
```

</details>

# Astrocytes in the dataset with all celltypes

## Load Seurat in from disk

The object `seu_spinal_allcelltypes_shortread_postQC.rds` was the object which \[name\] shared with me after her full QC.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-07-open-seurat
file_rds <- file.path(dir_data_in, "seu_shortread_allcelltypes_postQC.rds")
seu <- readRDS(file_rds)
# Test whether it loaded in correctly
seu
```

## Visualization annotation all celltypes

\[name\] defined major cell types using a publicly available atlas of the human spinal cord of the Allan Brain Insitute. These are stored in the columns `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass` and `predicted.id_coarse_allen_group`, with the latter having a more subdivided annotation than the former.

```{r}
#| label: fig-08-umap-subclass
#| fig-cap: "UMAP of all cell types, coloured by Allen subclass annotation"
# I want to show both subclass and cellclass. First show subclass
p_allen_subclass <- DimPlot(
  seu,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  NoLegend() +
  ggtitle("UMAP after filtering - Allen subclass")
p_allen_subclass
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-09-umap-cellclass
p_allen_group <- DimPlot(
  seu,
  reduction = "umap",
  group.by = "predicted.id_coarse_allen_group",
  label = TRUE,
  repel = TRUE
) +
  NoLegend() +
  ggtitle("UMAP after filtering - Allen Group")
p_allen_group
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-10-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plots, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_allen_subclass, "allcelltypes_umap_alansubclass")
save_plot(p_allen_group, "allcelltypes_umap_alangroup")
```


## Visualization astrocyte markers

I previously provided the annotation of celltypes, but I would like to confirm that the labelled astrocytes are astrocytes. A FeaturePlot() with astrocyte-marker genes forms a quick way to do so. In the default settings of this document, I provided the astrocyte marker genes `c("GFAP", "AQP4", "SLC1A2", "OBI1-AS1")`. You can see that the astrocyte cluster expresses these markers.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-11-featureplot
p_feature <- FeaturePlot(
  seu,
  features = astro_markers,
  reduction = "umap"
)
p_feature
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-12-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_feature, "allcelltypes_featureplot")
```

## Visualization astrocyte frequency

I want to show how many astrocytes each sample has. I will create multiple types of barplots.
- visualizations of proportional frequency and visualizations with relative frequency (as scRNAseq data is proportional)
- visualizations with the frequency of all celltypes vs visualizations with just astrocytes vs non-astrocytes

This section uses the functions `calc_freq` and `bar_freq`, which I created myself in the section **Helper functions**.

### Frequency of all cell types

I will visualize using the column `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass`, which is the same one as used in the first image under the header **Visualization annotation all celltypes**.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-13-preprocessing-freq
# Extract dataframe from seurat object
metadata <- seu@meta.data |>
  as.data.frame()
# Calculate frequencies of celltypes
freq_table <- calc_freq(
  metadata,
  "predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass",
  "AnonymousID"
)

# Show the top rows in the knitted file
kable(head(freq_table))
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-14-absolute-freq
p_abs <- bar_freq(freq_table, "stack")
p_abs
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-15-proportional-freq
p_prop <- bar_freq(freq_table, "fill")
p_prop
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-16-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_abs, "allcelltypes_barplot_abs")
save_plot(p_prop, "allcelltypes_barplot_prop")
```


### Frequency astrocyte vs non-astrocyte

```{r}
#| label: chunk-17-preprocessing-freq
# Make a column which states whether something is an astrocyte or not
metadata$astro <- ifelse(
  test = metadata$predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass == "Astrocytes",
  yes = "Astrocyte",
  no = "Non-Astrocyte"
)

# Calculate frequencies of astrocyte vs non-astrocyte per sample
freq_table <- calc_freq(metadata, "astro", "AnonymousID")

# Show the top rows in the knitted file
kable(head(freq_table))
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-18-absolute-freq
p_abs <- bar_freq(freq_table, "stack", just_astro = TRUE)
p_abs
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-19-proportional-freq
p_prop <- bar_freq(freq_table, "fill", just_astro = TRUE)
p_prop
```

```{r}
#| label: chunk-20-save-plots
#| echo: false
# Store the plot, but keep this hidden for the output
save_plot(p_abs, "allcelltypes_barplot_abs_just_astro")
save_plot(p_prop, "allcelltypes_barplot_prop_just_astro")
```

# Subset astrocytes and save on disk

Now that we have inspected the astrocytes in the whole dataset, I can subset the astrocytes which I will continue in the rest of the project. I wil subset the astrocytes as annotated in the column `predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass`, which was visualized in @fig-08-umap-subclass.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-21-subset-astros
seu_astros <- subset(
  seu,
  subset = predicted.id_coarse_allen_subclass == "Astrocytes"
)
# Inspect
seu_astros
```

Even though one could technically still call this a raw file (I have not done any preprocessing besides subsetting the astrocytes), I will store it in the folder `data/processed` rather than `data/raw`: I count the subsetting as preprocessing.

```{r}
#| label: chunk-22-save-to-disk
file_rds <- file.path(dir_data_out, "seu_shortread_astros_subset.rds")
saveRDS(seu_astros, file_rds)
```
